text:
David Pastrnak is doing what Boston needs from its captain: 28 points in 22 games, 10 goals, 11 on the power play, and a shot that tops out at 95 mph, 98th percentile in the league. His 8.85 expected goals (the quality of his chances) sit just under his 10 goals, so none of this is a heater.

His last ten games have been a Bruins roller coaster: two losses, four wins, three losses, then a 4-1 win in Detroit, where he had a goal and an assist. Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub counted that Pastrnak has seven goals and 13 points in eight games after a loss this season. He tends to answer.

Evolving-Hockey's numbers explain why his raw on-ice figures can look ordinary: last season he played with teammates in the bottom 10% by impact and drew competition in the 97th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 6.3 scoring chances per 60 from the slot area. Our projection range puts his season around 104 points. The question in Boston is who gives him help, not what he gives them.
headline: Pastrnak keeps the Bruins upright
